newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japanese businessman kidnapped in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Japanese businessman kidnapped in Philippines.

text.p: A Japanese businessman was kidnapped and a Filipino he was with shot dead by six heavily armed men in a beach resort in southern Philippines, local police said on Monday.

Kenichi Takayama was forcibly taken from the resort in Glan town, Saranggani province, 1,120 km (695 miles) southeast of Manila, on Sunday afternoon. He was with five Filipinos, one of whom was gunned down by the kidnappers when he tried to resist.
Takayama is registered as a resident of nearby General Santos city, a fledgling business district in southern Mindanao island, reports reaching the regional headquarters said.

A police official said that the armed men could have originally planned to rob the group, but decided to take hostages after killing one of them. The kidnappers fled into the rugged hills in Saranggani island.

Kidnapping remains a serious problem in the Philippines especially in the southern Philippines where Moslem separatists and pirates are known to operate. But this is the first known kidnapping of a foreigner so far this year.
A local anti-crime group estimates that an average of more than one person is kidnapped every day, often local Filipino-Chinese businessmen.
